teams.heading: Jake White says Fiji can be a massive force at World Cup
teams.body: Jake White has backed Fiji to make a real impact at next year's World Cup in Australia, saying that if he can assemble the best 33 players for the tournament, they "can be a massive force". The former Springbok coach made the case after Fiji's 34-28 win over Japan in Tokyo, a game he played without any Europe-based players and in which he handed out four new caps. White's view is that Fiji can beat anyone on their day, provided the squad gets control and structure.

lead.why: No NEW items in today's shortlist, and this is the team's own coach with a fresh World Cup angle that the Tuesday fixtures piece did not cover.

teams.heading: Fin Smith misses England training with calf injury ahead of Australia test
teams.body: Fin Smith, pencilled in as England's starting No 10, is missing training with a calf injury, and the timing could hardly be worse for Steve Borthwick. The two leading midfield candidates for the Australia test, Seb Atkinson and Bernhard Janse van Rensburg, are also unable to train this week, while Bath flanker Guy Pepper limped off against Gloucester. Borthwick's November now has to deliver lasting answers as well as results.

lead.why: The highest-scoring NEW item, and it concerns England's own squad fitness and selection ahead of the Australia test.

teams.heading: Galthié reshuffles squad after injuries to Hastoy, Gazzotti and Brau-Boirie
teams.body: Fabien Galthié has reshuffled his extended squad for the Nations Championship after Antoine Hastoy, Marko Gazzotti and Fabien Brau-Boirie picked up injuries in Top 14 action and will miss the resumption of the competition. Nicolas Depoortere, Anthony Jelonch and Louis Le Brun have been called up, and the Castres fly-half could win his first cap. Planet Rugby counts four withdrawals in all, on top of absences for Jalibert, Ramos and Marchand.

lead.why: It is the team's own squad story, not in the already-reported list, and it is the most concrete France news in today's pack.

teams.heading: Garry Ringrose ruled out of Ireland's November Tests with hamstring injury
teams.body: Garry Ringrose is unlikely to be involved in Ireland's three home Nations Championship Tests, the IRFU said on Tuesday, and will continue his hamstring rehabilitation with Leinster. The 31-year-old, who has 76 caps, missed Leinster's URC win over Munster at the weekend. Andy Farrell has decided against calling up any replacements, despite uncertainty over Tadhg Furlong's availability. Sam Prendergast remains a doubt for the Argentina opener with a wrist injury.

lead.why: The highest-scoring NEW story about Ireland's own squad, carried by BBC and Planet Rugby, and it is a different story from the O'Brien concussion item already reported.

teams.heading: Menoncello set to miss autumn Tests after Toulouse shoulder sprain
teams.body: Italy's centre Tommaso Menoncello is set to miss the autumn Tests after a left shoulder sprain suffered for Toulouse, with the injury expected to keep him out for several weeks. He went off in the 43rd minute of Toulouse's 43-40 Champions Cup win over Exeter Chiefs. It is another setback for the 24-year-old, who joined Toulouse over the summer and had already been sidelined after an early-season injury. Gonzalo Quesada must prepare for the November campaign, starting against South Africa, without one of his key backs.

lead.why: It is the only shortlisted item about an Italy player's injury, and the other candidates are sevens, a months-old piece or a story already covered.

teams.heading: Townsend insists Scotland now believe they can beat the All Blacks
teams.body: Gregor Townsend says Scotland now believe they can beat New Zealand, a feeling his playing generation never had. Recalling the 62-31 and 69-20 defeats he suffered as a player, he told the BBC's Scotland Rugby Podcast: "It's almost like two different lifetimes." As coach he has faced the All Blacks three times, all in Edinburgh, losing 25-17, 31-23 and 22-17. He concedes Scotland may have lacked composure in those games, but says the belief is there.

lead.why: It is a NEW item about Scotland's head coach, carries substantive detail, and gives the fan a clear talking point ahead of the All Blacks game.

teams.heading: Macs Page called up as Rio Dyer ruled out of autumn
teams.body: Rio Dyer has been released from the Wales squad with a hamstring injury picked up while scoring for the Dragons at Ospreys. The door opens for uncapped Scarlets wing Macs Page, who was left out of the original squad despite four tries in his first four matches. Page is in return-to-play protocols after a head injury against the Stormers, and Wales kicking coach Alex Davies said of Dyer: "To be selected and then get an injury is tough."

lead.why: A fresh squad change that hands Wales a debut opportunity, and it is a different story from the three already reported.

teams.heading: Thomas Gallo sidelined at least six months as Pumas make three changes
teams.body: Felipe Contepomi's London mini-camp has been rebuilt after three injury-enforced changes. Prop Thomas Gallo dislocated his left wrist in Lyon's win at Bayonne and will be sidelined for at least six months after an operation; Dragons loosehead Rodrigo Martínez replaces him. Santiago Carreras, out with a knee injury, has been replaced by Mateo Soler. Santiago Chocobares, concussed, awaits the outcome of an HIA, with Matías Moroni on standby ahead of the Ireland opener.

lead.why: It is the most corroborated item in the pack and concerns Argentina's own squad, with a long-term injury and two replacements.

teams.heading: Angus Crichton signs with NSW Waratahs for 2027 after switching from league
teams.body: Angus Crichton, a Kangaroos and Blues Origin star, has committed to the NSW Waratahs for 2027, a switch from the NRL that Rugby Australia unveiled in January. The 29-year-old grew up playing union and came close to joining the Western Force after the 2023 World Cup. His contract is understood to be around $650,000 and carries a get-out clause after the 2027 World Cup. He will link up with former Roosters teammate Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii once the 2026 NRL season ends.

lead.why: It is the only Wallabies-side story in the pack, and the others are either already run (the Bledisloe MCG item), England's injury news, or sevens-style Deaf rugby.

teams.heading: Kwagga Smith leaves Shizuoka Blue Revs for three-year Bulls contract
teams.body: Kwagga Smith's time in Japan is over: the Shizuoka Blue Revs announced his contract had been terminated by 'mutual agreement', and the 33-year-old, a two-time World Cup winner with more than 60 Tests for South Africa, has signed a three-year deal with the Bulls. The back-rower, who spent eight seasons at the club since 2018, tore his ACL and meniscus in May and was ruled out for the rest of 2026. Ackermann, his former Lions coach, praised him: "He's a team man who has grown into a stalwart".

lead.why: The only shortlist item that is men's XV and not already reported; it is a Japan club story, though a background one.

teams.heading: Rennie confirms Richie Mo'unga will miss Scotland but is likely for Wales
teams.body: Richie Mo'unga will miss the Scotland Test, with Dave Rennie confirming the flyhalf is not yet ready after the calf tear he suffered in training ahead of the first Bledisloe Cup Test. Rennie is more optimistic about Wales: "Richie won’t be available for Scotland," he said at the squad announcement, adding that he is "a good chance for Wales." Mo'unga was taken to Sydney so the MedFit staff could build him up, and he has run well over the past week.

teams.heading: Cheslin Kolbe set to miss rest of Nations Championship with broken jaw
teams.body: Cheslin Kolbe is set to miss the rest of the Nations Championship with a broken jaw, the sharpest blow in a crocked week for the world champions. André Esterhuizen limped off after barely a minute in Cardiff, Handré Pollard came a cropper at Loftus, and Venter and Fourie were forced off in the Stormers' win. Concerns remain over Eben Etzebeth (leg), Vusi Moyo (shoulder) and Ben-Jason Dixon (concussion symptoms), with Italy, Ireland and France still to come.

lead.why: The only item about the Springboks' own players, and it covers the biggest availability problem in the squad.
